blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The constitutional history of India is broadly divided into Company Rule (1773–1858) and Crown Rule (1858–1947).
The Regulating Act of 1773 designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta.
The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, centralizing administrative power.
The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for an All-India Federation and divided powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent lists.
The Indian Independence Act of 1947 ended British rule and declared India an independent sovereign state.
Distinction between Dyarchy in Provinces (introduced by Montford Reforms 1919) and Dyarchy at the Centre (proposed by GoI Act 1935).
Establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta under the Regulating Act of 1773 versus the Federal Court under the GoI Act of 1935.
Introduction of open competition for selection of civil servants via the Charter Act of 1853.
